questions.question: Why does Tomasz agree to the costly options at the funeral home?
answers: Because he had compared all the offers beforehand
Because in his grief he trusts that the proposed elements are necessary for a dignified farewell
Because he had special insurance
Because his mother had left everything in her will
questions.explanation: The text shows his confusion and vulnerability to suggestion at the moment of a fresh loss.

questions.question: What most changes his outlook a few weeks later?
answers: A newspaper article about cremation
A conversation with Magda about cheaper and ecological alternatives
A phone call from the bank
A letter from the priest
questions.explanation: Magda is the first to make him realise that other solutions existed.

questions.question: What role does the Funerarium foundation meeting play?
answers: It convinces him to buy a more expensive urn
It shows that a family has the right to ask, to choose and to complain about a badly performed service
It forbids children from taking part in funerals
It urges him to move house
questions.explanation: Agnes Tołoczmańska talks about the right to choose and about consumer rights.

questions.question: What broader change does Tomasz make after this education?
answers: He stops visiting the cemetery
He starts talking with loved ones, including children, about death and funeral choices
He sets up a funeral company
He gives up reading books
questions.explanation: After the reading and the meeting he begins to make the topic of death familiar within his family.

questions.question: What main conclusion closes Tomasz's story?
answers: It's best never to arrange funerals on your own
In a situation of ignorance you must ask and demand alternatives
A high price always means dignity
Children should not know about death
questions.explanation: The final reflection comes down to the right to ask questions and to choose.
